name: WV-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's partisan lean is roughly 22 points Republican, among the reddest House seats
Carol Miller is a well-funded incumbent with about $2.0 million raised and $505,000 on hand
Democrat Vince George has raised only $311,000 and reported just $3,138 cash on hand
Prediction markets price Miller's win probability near 97-98 percent
model.rationale: The district's deep Republican lean, Miller's incumbency, and her overwhelming financial advantage over a nearly cash-free challenger leave no evidence of competitiveness. Prediction markets and the absence of any serious polling attention both point to a comfortable Republican hold.
model.watch: Only a major late-breaking scandal or an unusually large national wave against Republicans could put this seat in play, and nothing in the current evidence suggests either.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
West Virginia's first district is one of the most Republican-leaning House seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly 22 points toward the GOP. Carol Miller, the incumbent, is running for another term after securing renomination. She has raised about $2 million and holds more than $500,000 in cash, while Democratic nominee Vince George has raised roughly $300,000 and reported only about $3,000 on hand. No public general-election polls are available, and no major expert raters have flagged the race as competitive.

Prediction markets give Miller roughly a 97 to 98 percent chance of winning, consistent with the district's fundamentals. A Constitution Party candidate is also on the ballot but has shown no measurable fundraising or spending. Absent an extraordinary development, the seat is expected to remain in Republican hands by a wide margin in November.
